description: Read, write, compare, and order multi-digit whole numbers using place-value understanding.
Round whole numbers to any place and use rounding to estimate sums and differences.
Fluently add and subtract multi-digit whole numbers using the standard algorithm.
Interpret multiplication as equal groups and arrays and fluently recall products of one-digit factors.
Interpret division as equal sharing or grouping and use fact families to divide within 100.
Multiply multi-digit whole numbers using place-value strategies and the standard algorithm.
Divide multi-digit whole numbers by one- and two-digit divisors and interpret remainders in context.
Find factor pairs and multiples and classify whole numbers as prime or composite.
Understand unit fractions as equal parts of a whole and locate fractions on the number line.
Read, write, compare, and round decimals to thousandths using place-value understanding.
Add and subtract fractions and mixed numbers, including with unlike denominators.
Multiply fractions by whole numbers and by fractions, including in area contexts.
Divide unit fractions by whole numbers and whole numbers by unit fractions using models.
Add, subtract, multiply, and divide decimals to hundredths using place-value strategies.
Generate and recognize equivalent fractions using visual models and multiplication.
Compare fractions with different numerators and denominators using benchmarks and common denominators.
Interpret and solve problems where one quantity is a whole-number times as much as another.
Write fractions with denominators 10 and 100 as decimals and compare quantities across notations.
Interpret multiplication as scaling and predict whether a product is larger or smaller than its factors.
Convert among units within the same measurement system to solve multi-step problems.
Interpret the equal sign as 'has the same value as' and decide whether equations are true or false.
Apply commutative, associative, and distributive properties to compute flexibly and check results.
Find the unknown whole number in addition, subtraction, multiplication, or division equations.
Represent two-step word problems with equations using a letter for the unknown and assess reasonableness.
Evaluate numerical expressions containing parentheses, brackets, and braces.
Write and interpret numerical expressions from verbal descriptions without evaluating them.
Identify and explain arithmetic patterns in addition and multiplication tables.
Generate a number or shape pattern that follows a given rule and identify features of the pattern.
Complete input-output tables and describe the rule relating inputs to outputs.
Generate two numerical patterns from rules and identify relationships between corresponding terms.
Form ordered pairs from two related patterns and graph them in the first quadrant.
Classify quadrilaterals and other polygons by shared attributes such as sides and angles.
Find perimeters of polygons, including finding an unknown side length from the perimeter.
Understand area as covering with unit squares and find rectangle areas by multiplying side lengths.
Identify points, lines, rays, parallel and perpendicular lines, and acute, right, and obtuse angles.
Measure and sketch angles in degrees and solve additive angle problems.
Identify lines of symmetry and complete or draw figures with line symmetry.
Classify two-dimensional figures in a hierarchy based on their properties.
Understand volume as packing unit cubes and compute volumes of rectangular prisms.
Graph and interpret points in the first quadrant of the coordinate plane.
Draw and interpret scaled picture graphs and bar graphs and solve one- and two-step data questions.
Make line plots with fractional measurements and answer questions using operations on the data.
Read and interpret line graphs that show how a quantity changes over time.
Describe events as certain, likely, unlikely, or impossible and compare chances informally.
Fluently add, subtract, multiply, and divide multi-digit decimals using standard algorithms.
Divide fractions by fractions using models and algorithms and interpret quotients in context.
Find greatest common factors and least common multiples and use the distributive property to rewrite sums.
Understand positive and negative numbers, opposites, and absolute value on the number line.
Order and compare rational numbers and interpret inequality statements in real-world contexts.
Add and subtract integers and other signed rationals using number lines and additive inverses.
Multiply and divide signed numbers and apply sign rules to evaluate expressions.
Solve multi-step problems using the four operations on positive and negative rational numbers.
Apply properties of integer exponents, including negative exponents, to generate equivalent expressions.
Express and compute with very large and very small quantities using scientific notation.
Evaluate square and cube roots and classify and approximate irrational numbers on the number line.
Understand ratios and use ratio language to describe relationships between quantities.
Generate and use equivalent ratios with tables, tape diagrams, and double number lines.
Compute and interpret unit rates, including rates with fractional quantities.
Find a percent of a quantity and find the whole given a part and the percent.
Decide whether two quantities are proportional and identify the constant of proportionality.
Write and solve proportion equations for multi-step real-world ratio problems.
Solve percent problems involving tax, tip, discount, markup, simple interest, and percent change.
Solve problems involving scale drawings, computing actual lengths and areas from a scale factor.
Write, read, and evaluate algebraic expressions with variables, including whole-number exponents.
Apply properties of operations to generate equivalent expressions and combine like terms.
Solve one-step equations in one variable and check solutions by substitution.
Write, interpret, and graph simple inequalities of the form x > c or x < c on the number line.
Solve two-step equations, including equations with rational number coefficients.
Expand and factor linear expressions with rational coefficients using the distributive property.
Solve and graph two-step inequalities and interpret the solution set in context.
Solve linear equations with variables on both sides, including cases with no or infinitely many solutions.
Solve pairs of simultaneous linear equations by graphing and substitution and interpret solutions.
Analyze relationships between independent and dependent variables using tables, graphs, and equations.
Understand a function as a rule that assigns exactly one output to each input.
Interpret slope as a unit rate and derive it from graphs, tables, and similar triangles.
Graph and interpret linear equations in the form y = mx + b, identifying slope and intercept.
Compare properties of two functions each represented in a different way, such as table versus graph.
Classify functions as linear or nonlinear and sketch or describe qualitative graph behavior.
Find areas of triangles, special quadrilaterals, and composite figures by composing and decomposing.
Represent solids with nets and compute surface areas of prisms and pyramids.
Find volumes of right rectangular prisms with fractional edge lengths using V = lwh.
Graph points in all four quadrants and find distances between points that share a coordinate.
Use complementary, supplementary, vertical, and adjacent angles, triangle angle sums, and parallel-line transversal angles to find unknown measures.
Know and apply the formulas for circumference and area of a circle.
Describe translations, rotations, reflections, and dilations, including coordinate effects, and use them to establish congruence and similarity.
Apply the Pythagorean theorem to find side lengths and distances in the coordinate plane.
Use volume formulas for cylinders, cones, and spheres to solve real-world problems.
Recognize statistical questions and describe distributions by center, spread, and overall shape.
Display numerical data in dot plots, histograms, and box plots and choose an appropriate display.
Compute and interpret mean, median, range, interquartile range, and mean absolute deviation.
Use data from random samples to draw and compare informal inferences about populations.
Find and interpret probabilities of simple events and compare predictions with experimental results.
Find probabilities of compound events using organized lists, tables, tree diagrams, and simulation.
Construct and interpret scatter plots and two-way tables and informally fit lines to linear data.
Classify real numbers as rational or irrational and reason about sums and products of the two types.
Apply product, quotient, power, zero, and negative exponent rules to simplify expressions with integer exponents.
Rewrite square roots in simplest radical form by extracting perfect-square factors.
Add, subtract, and multiply square-root expressions, combining like radicals and simplifying products.
Convert rates and units using conversion factors and choose appropriate units when modeling.
Compute slope from graphs, tables, and points and interpret it as a unit rate in context.
Identify, write, and solve direct variation models y = kx from tables, graphs, and word problems.
Compute repeated percent increase or decrease and express it with growth or decay factors.
Solve linear equations with distribution, fractions, and variables on both sides, identifying no-solution and identity cases.
Solve a formula or literal equation for a specified variable.
Solve and graph multi-step linear inequalities, reversing the symbol when multiplying or dividing by a negative.
Solve and graph conjunction (and) and disjunction (or) compound inequalities in one variable.
Solve absolute value equations by splitting into two cases and checking for extraneous results.
Solve systems of two linear equations by graphing and classify them as one solution, none, or infinitely many.
Solve linear systems by substitution, including setting up systems from word problems.
Solve linear systems by elimination, multiplying one or both equations when needed.
Add and subtract polynomials by combining like terms and writing results in standard form.
Multiply monomials, binomials, and trinomials, including squaring binomials.
Factor out the greatest common monomial factor and factor four-term polynomials by grouping.
Factor trinomials of the form x^2 + bx + c, including those with negative coefficients.
Factor trinomials ax^2 + bx + c with a > 1 using the ac method or guess-and-check.
Recognize and factor differences of squares and perfect-square trinomials.
Solve quadratic equations using factoring and the zero product property.
Solve quadratics by taking square roots and by completing the square, giving exact radical answers.
Solve quadratics with the quadratic formula and use the discriminant to count real solutions.
Decide whether a relation is a function and evaluate and interpret f(x) notation in context.
Determine the domain and range of a function from graphs, tables, and contexts.
Graph linear functions from slope-intercept and standard form, identifying slope and intercepts.
Write equations of lines from a slope and point, two points, or parallel and perpendicular conditions.
Graph two-variable linear inequalities and systems of inequalities, identifying the solution region.
Write recursive and explicit rules for arithmetic sequences and connect them to linear functions.
Write recursive and explicit rules for geometric sequences and connect them to exponential functions.
Write and evaluate exponential growth and decay functions y = a(b)^x from contexts.
Graph exponential functions, identifying intercepts, asymptotes, and end behavior.
Graph quadratics, identifying vertex, axis of symmetry, intercepts, and maximum or minimum.
Describe and graph vertical and horizontal shifts, reflections, and stretches of parent functions.
Compute average rate of change over an interval and compare linear, exponential, and quadratic growth.
Use the distance and midpoint formulas to compute lengths and midpoints in the coordinate plane.
Represent perimeter, area, and volume of figures with polynomial expressions and evaluate them.
Compare distributions using shape, center, spread, standard deviation, and the effect of outliers.
Build two-way tables and interpret joint, marginal, and conditional relative frequencies.
Make scatter plots, fit a linear model, and interpret its slope and intercept in context.
Use residuals and the correlation coefficient to judge fit, and distinguish correlation from causation.
Compute exact lengths and areas involving square roots and simplify radical answers.
Convert linear, square, and cubic units and report answers with appropriate precision.
Perform dilations from a center, find scale factors, and describe their effect on segments and angles.
Use similarity statements and proportional side lengths to find missing measures in similar figures.
Establish triangle similarity with AA, SAS, and SSS criteria and use it to solve for unknown lengths.
Apply the side-splitter, midsegment, and angle-bisector proportionality theorems.
Use sine, cosine, and tangent ratios to find missing side lengths in right triangles.
Use inverse trig ratios to find angles, including angle-of-elevation and depression problems.
Predict how a scale factor k changes perimeter, area, and volume of similar figures and solids.
Write and evaluate conditionals, converses, inverses, contrapositives, and biconditionals.
Form conjectures from patterns, find counterexamples, and apply the laws of detachment and syllogism.
Justify each step of solving an equation using properties of equality in two-column form.
Prove basic theorems about segments and angles, such as vertical angles and congruent supplements.
Prove and apply theorems about angles formed by parallel lines and transversals, including converses.
Decide whether triangles are congruent using SSS, SAS, ASA, AAS, and HL, connecting each to rigid motions.
Write triangle congruence proofs and use CPCTC to prove segments and angles congruent.
Prove properties of parallelograms and the tests that classify special quadrilaterals.
Use slope, distance, and midpoint to prove properties of figures placed on the coordinate plane.
Represent translations, reflections, rotations, and dilations as coordinate functions (x, y) -> (x', y').
Express area, volume, or cost as a function of a single dimension and use it to optimize a design.
Compute lengths and angle measures using segment addition, angle addition, and bisectors.
Solve problems using complementary, supplementary, vertical, and linear-pair angle relationships.
Find angle measures formed by parallel lines and transversals using alternate, corresponding, and co-interior angles.
Apply the triangle angle-sum and exterior-angle theorems, including with isosceles and equilateral triangles.
Use the triangle inequality and side-angle relationships to test side lengths and order sides and angles.
Apply perpendicular bisector and angle bisector theorems and locate the centroid, circumcenter, and incenter.
Perform and identify translations, reflections, and rotations that carry a figure onto another.
Compose transformations and identify line and rotational symmetry of figures.
Compute interior and exterior angle measures and sums for polygons.
Use properties of parallelograms, rectangles, rhombi, squares, trapezoids, and kites to find measures.
Apply the Pythagorean theorem and its converse to solve problems and classify triangles.
Use 45-45-90 and 30-60-90 relationships to find exact side lengths.
Find measures of central angles, inscribed angles, arcs, and chords in circles.
Apply angle and segment relationships formed by tangents, secants, and chords.
Compute arc length and sector area and describe radian measure as a ratio of arc to radius.
Write and graph circle equations (x-h)^2 + (y-k)^2 = r^2, completing the square when needed.
Find areas of triangles, quadrilaterals, regular polygons, and composite figures.
Compute surface area and volume of prisms and cylinders, including composite solids.
Compute surface area and volume of pyramids, cones, and spheres.
Identify cross-sections of solids, solids of revolution, and apply Cavalieri's principle.
Describe sample spaces and compute theoretical and experimental probabilities and complements.
Compute probabilities of unions, intersections, and independent or dependent events using addition and multiplication rules.
Compute conditional probabilities from two-way tables and test events for independence.
Compute probabilities as ratios of lengths, areas, or angle measures.
Evaluate and simplify nth roots and higher-index radical expressions.
Convert between radical and rational-exponent forms and simplify using exponent properties.
Add, multiply, and divide radical expressions, rationalizing denominators including conjugates.
Simplify square roots of negative numbers and evaluate powers of i.
Add, subtract, multiply, and divide complex numbers using conjugates.
Write and solve inverse, joint, and combined variation models from data and contexts.
Compute compound interest with n compoundings and continuously, comparing effective growth rates.
Set up and solve work, mixture, and motion problems that lead to rational equations.
Solve absolute value inequalities and express solutions in interval notation.
Solve systems of three linear equations in three variables by elimination and substitution.
Complete the square to solve quadratics and to convert between standard and vertex form.
Solve quadratics with the quadratic formula, including complex solutions, and interpret the discriminant.
Solve quadratic inequalities in one variable using critical values and sign analysis.
Solve linear-quadratic and quadratic-quadratic systems algebraically and graphically.
Add, subtract, and multiply higher-degree polynomials, including binomial expansion with Pascal's triangle.
Divide polynomials using long division and synthetic division.
Apply the remainder and factor theorems to evaluate polynomials and verify factors.
Factor cubics and quartics using grouping, sum and difference of cubes, and quadratic form.
Solve polynomial equations by factoring and the rational root theorem, counting roots with multiplicity.
Solve radical and rational-exponent equations, identifying extraneous solutions.
Simplify, multiply, and divide rational expressions, stating excluded values.
Add and subtract rational expressions with unlike denominators and simplify complex fractions.
Solve rational equations by clearing denominators and rejecting extraneous solutions.
Solve exponential equations by matching common bases and by taking logarithms.
Expand and condense logarithmic expressions using product, quotient, power, and change-of-base rules.
Solve logarithmic equations using properties of logs and check for extraneous solutions.
Add, subtract, multiply, and divide functions and evaluate the results, attending to domain.
Compose functions, evaluate compositions, and decompose a function into simpler parts.
Find and verify inverse functions algebraically and graphically, restricting domains when needed.
Graph a f(b(x - h)) + k transformations across parent function families.
Evaluate and graph piecewise-defined, step, and absolute value functions.
Predict end behavior of polynomial graphs from degree and leading coefficient.
Sketch polynomial graphs using zeros, multiplicity, and turning points.
Graph square-root and cube-root functions and determine their domains and ranges.
Graph rational functions, identifying vertical and horizontal asymptotes, holes, and intercepts.
Graph and analyze exponential functions, including base e, growth versus decay, and asymptotes.
Define logarithms as inverses of exponentials, evaluate logs, and graph logarithmic functions.
Model half-life, doubling time, and continuous growth, solving for time with logarithms.
Evaluate arithmetic, finite geometric, and convergent infinite geometric series using sigma notation.
Convert between degrees and radians and evaluate sine, cosine, and tangent at unit-circle angles.
Graph sine and cosine functions, identifying amplitude, period, midline, and phase shift.
Write sinusoidal models for periodic phenomena and interpret their parameters.
Derive and use the equation of a parabola from its focus and directrix.
Write and graph equations of circles, ellipses, and hyperbolas by completing the square.
Distinguish surveys, experiments, and observational studies and identify sources of bias in sampling.
Use the empirical rule and z-scores to estimate proportions under a normal curve.
Use simulation to estimate margins of error and judge whether a difference is plausibly due to chance.
Count outcomes using the fundamental counting principle, permutations, and combinations.
Compute binomial probabilities with combinations and find the expected value of a random process.
Add, subtract, multiply, and divide complex numbers, including powers of i and use of conjugates.
Plot complex numbers in the complex plane, find modulus and argument, and convert between rectangular and trigonometric form.
Use De Moivre's theorem to compute powers and nth roots of complex numbers in polar form.
Define the radian as an arc-to-radius ratio, convert between degrees and radians, and compute arc length s = rθ.
Relate angular speed and linear speed for circular motion and solve rate problems involving rotating objects.
Use the Law of Sines to solve oblique triangles, including analysis of the ambiguous case.
Use the Law of Cosines and the area formula (1/2)ab·sin C to solve and measure oblique triangles.
Divide polynomials using long or synthetic division and apply the Remainder and Factor Theorems.
Find all real and complex zeros of a polynomial using the Fundamental Theorem of Algebra and conjugate pairs.
Solve polynomial and rational inequalities using sign charts and zero/undefined boundary analysis.
Expand, condense, and evaluate logarithmic expressions using product, quotient, power, and change-of-base rules.
Solve exponential and logarithmic equations, checking for extraneous solutions from domain restrictions.
Simplify expressions and verify identities using Pythagorean, reciprocal, quotient, and even-odd identities.
Apply sum, difference, and double-angle formulas to evaluate expressions and verify identities.
Solve trigonometric equations on a given interval and express general solutions using periodicity.
Add, scale, and multiply matrices, attending to dimension compatibility and non-commutativity.
Compute 2×2 determinants and inverses and use inverse matrices to solve linear systems.
Compute average rates of change over intervals and describe where functions increase, decrease, or change concavity.
Graph and write functions built from parent functions using combined shifts, stretches, and reflections.
Compose functions, determine domains of compositions, and decompose a function into simpler components.
Find and verify inverse functions, restrict domains for invertibility, and relate graphs across the line y = x.
Analyze polynomial graphs using end behavior with limit notation, zeros with multiplicity, and local extrema.
Graph rational functions by identifying holes, vertical and horizontal or slant asymptotes, and intercepts.
Analyze power functions with rational exponents, including inverse variation, symmetry, and end behavior.
Graph and interpret exponential growth and decay functions, including base e and compound interest models.
Define logarithms as inverses of exponentials, evaluate logs, and graph logarithmic functions with domain analysis.
Write explicit forms of arithmetic and geometric sequences and connect them to linear and exponential functions.
Graph sine and cosine functions and identify amplitude, period, midline, and phase shift from graphs or equations.
Graph tangent, cotangent, secant, and cosecant functions, identifying period, asymptotes, and range.
Evaluate inverse sine, cosine, and tangent using restricted domains and compose trig with inverse trig functions.
Graph parametric curves, eliminate the parameter, and interpret parametric equations as planar motion.
Graph polar functions such as circles, roses, and limaçons and describe how r changes as θ varies.
Use the unit circle to find exact sine, cosine, and tangent values for special angles in all quadrants.
Plot points in polar coordinates and convert points and simple equations between rectangular and polar form.
Express vectors in component form, compute magnitude and direction, and perform addition and scalar multiplication.
Use unit vectors, dot products, and vector sums to model force, velocity, and navigation problems.
Interpret 2×2 matrices as linear transformations of the plane and the determinant as an area scaling factor.
Identify and graph circles, ellipses, parabolas, and hyperbolas from standard-form equations.
Choose an appropriate function type for a data set or context using growth patterns, residuals, and domain constraints.
Fit exponential models to data and use semi-log plots to recognize and linearize exponential relationships.
Build sinusoidal models from periodic data or contexts such as tides and temperatures, and use them to predict values.
Compare the relative magnitudes of logarithmic, polynomial, and exponential expressions in limits at infinity.
Recognize 0/0 and ∞/∞ indeterminate forms and apply L'Hopital's rule after verifying its conditions.
Interpret the meaning and units of a derivative in applied contexts as an instantaneous rate of change.
Set up equations relating changing quantities and differentiate with respect to time to solve related-rates problems.
Use tangent-line approximations and differentials to estimate values and classify over- or underestimates via concavity.
Evaluate limits by factoring, rationalizing, and combining fractions to resolve 0/0 indeterminate forms algebraically.
Solve for parameter values that make piecewise-defined functions continuous or differentiable at a boundary.
Differentiate relations defined implicitly, solve for dy/dx, and find tangent lines to implicit curves.
Rewrite integrands using algebraic manipulation, long division, and identities to match basic antiderivative forms.
Estimate limits and one-sided limits from graphs and tables and decide when a limit fails to exist.
Evaluate limits using limit properties, direct substitution, and limits of composite functions.
Apply the squeeze theorem and the special limits of sin(x)/x and (1−cos x)/x as x approaches 0.
Evaluate infinite limits and limits at infinity and connect them to vertical and horizontal asymptotes.
Apply the three-part definition of continuity and classify removable, jump, and infinite discontinuities.
Use the Intermediate Value Theorem to justify the existence of solutions on an interval for continuous functions.
Define the derivative as a limit of difference quotients and compute derivatives at a point and as a function.
Determine where a function is differentiable, relate differentiability to continuity, and sketch f′ from the graph of f.
Differentiate using power, sum, and constant-multiple rules along with derivatives of sin x, cos x, e^x, and ln x.
Differentiate products and quotients of functions, including the remaining trigonometric derivatives.
Differentiate composite functions with the chain rule, including combinations with product and quotient rules.
Differentiate inverse functions using the reciprocal relationship and find derivatives of inverse trig functions.
Compute and notate second and higher derivatives and interpret the second derivative as the rate of change of a rate.
Analyze position, velocity, acceleration, and speed for particles in rectilinear motion using derivatives.
Verify hypotheses and apply the Mean Value Theorem and Rolle's Theorem to draw conclusions about derivatives.
Find critical points and use the Extreme Value Theorem and candidates test to locate absolute extrema on closed intervals.
Use the sign of f′ to determine intervals of increase and decrease and classify relative extrema.
Use the sign of f″ to determine concavity and inflection points and apply the second derivative test.
Move among the graphs and behaviors of f, f′, and f″ to sketch curves and justify features of each.
Model applied problems with a function of one variable and use derivative tests to find and justify optimal values.
Find general antiderivatives using basic rules and solve for constants of integration from initial conditions.
Express definite integrals as limits of Riemann sums and apply linearity and interval-splitting properties.
Evaluate definite integrals using antiderivatives via the Fundamental Theorem of Calculus.
Analyze functions defined by integrals, using FTC Part 1 to differentiate them and integrand graphs to describe behavior.
Evaluate indefinite and definite integrals by substitution, including changing limits of integration.
Compute the average value of a function on an interval and connect it to the Mean Value Theorem for integrals.
Verify solutions to differential equations and sketch or match slope fields to equations and solution curves.
Solve separable differential equations with initial conditions, including exponential growth and decay models dy/dt = ky.
Interpret definite integrals of rates as net change and solve rate-in/rate-out accumulation problems.
Use integrals of velocity and acceleration to find displacement, total distance traveled, and position.
Set up and evaluate integrals for regions between curves, integrating with respect to x or y as appropriate.
Compute volumes of solids with known cross sections such as squares, semicircles, and triangles on a planar base.
Compute volumes of solids of revolution using disk and washer methods about horizontal and vertical axes.
Estimate derivatives from tabular data using difference quotients over the smallest available intervals.
Approximate definite integrals from tables or graphs using left, right, midpoint, and trapezoidal sums, classifying over- and underestimates.
